Team — Sara from PayDrop reported a material 503 spike during their morning peak (08:50–09:05 PDT). They provided logs and a screenshot. I need a quick triage so we can: 1) confirm the exact exposure window, 2) determine SLO credit eligibility, and 3) schedule a postmortem and remediation timeline.

Initial asks:
- Jordan: please prioritize the runtime traces (kvcache, auth proxy, and routing) for 08:40–09:15 PDT (us-west-2). Look for cache miss storms or auth token timeouts that could produce 503s.
- Diego: coordinate with telemetry to pull token-level error breakdown and router logs; include any 429/503 correlation.
- Laura: if this is an availability hit, prepare a communications draft for PayDrop procurement and a proposed prorated credit calculation methodology.

I attached Sara's sample log and the Grafana screenshot she sent. Also attaching a request-for-logs checklist we use for SLA evaluations.

Attachments: paydrop-checkout-503-sample.log, impact-summary-screencap.png, request-for-logs.pdf

I'll own external comms. Please reply with ETA and first observations. If you find this is a cross-region failover or routing issue, escalate to infra immediately.

—Evelyn
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Jenkins <sara.jenkins@paydrop.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Sep 2025 17:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: PayDrop checkout 503 spike — initial verification

Sara — thanks again for the artifacts and patience while we dug in. Summary of our initial verification below.

What we confirmed:
- Exposure window: 2025-09-09 08:49:30 — 09:04:10 PDT (UTC-7).
- Symptom: elevated 503 responses originating from the auth proxy layer that cascaded into request routing failures.
- Root cause (preliminary): transient KV cache eviction pattern combined with auth token refresh storms for a small subset of tenants that caused short-lived overload on the auth proxy pool. This produced a ~10–13% failure rate for requests routed through the affected proxies.

Attachments: paydrop-traces.zip (trace bundle), a short timeline (csv) and an impact snippet sampled from your log.

Next steps and timeline:
- We're opening a formal postmortem; internal owner: Jordan Blake (infra). Draft due in 72 hours (EOD Mon).
- Credit eligibility: based on preliminary timeline and your contract (PD-8472), this looks like an availability degradation eligible for prorated credit. Laura will run the exact calculation and follow up with a credit quote within 48 hours.
- Remediation: immediate mitigation (increasing auth-proxy pool and hardening cache eviction) applied the same day; long-term fix (KV eviction gating + better token refresh backoff) targeted in the next sprint.

If PayDrop can share any additional request IDs or synthetic checks that failed in that window it will help tighten our effect calculation.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll get you a formal postmortem and a proposed credit in the timeline above.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai
